subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should idle/age sandbox prune delete non-shared local sandbox workspaces as part of this bug fix now, or should workspace deletion wait for the managed session-owned lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but deleting host workspace directories is a destructive sandbox/session-state decision that must preserve active, shared, agent-scoped, browser, SSH, and OpenShell ownership semantics.

options.title: Land narrow owner-safe cleanup
options.body: Approve a focused backend-aware cleanup that deletes only confirmed-unused non-shared workspaces after successful runtime removal, with focused Docker/SSH/OpenShell coverage.

options.title: Defer to managed lifecycle
options.body: Keep this bug linked to the managed lifecycle work and close it only after the broader session-owned cleanup contract lands.

options.title: Preserve workspaces by contract
options.body: Decide that prune/recreate should remove runtimes only, then update docs/doctor to provide an explicit workspace cleanup or reset path.

recommendation.title: Land narrow owner-safe cleanup
recommendation.body: Approve a focused backend-aware cleanup that deletes only confirmed-unused non-shared workspaces after successful runtime removal, with focused Docker/SSH/OpenShell coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the active managed sandbox lifecycle issue/PR that already frames the product and security tradeoff for owner-matched cleanup.
